title: AO/696/2016 of Smt. Vedwati AND OTHERS Vs Yogendra Singh AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Appeal from Order No. 696 of 2016
Smt. Vedwati & Others Ö. Appellants
Versus
Yogendra Singh & Others Ö. Respondents

Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate for the appellants.
Mr. A.S. Rawat, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. P.C. Petshali, Advocate for respondent no. 4.
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Having heard the rival contentions on the stay
vacation application moved on behalf of defendant no. 5-
Shri Prashant Arora, it transpires that original suit no.
3/2014 was instituted by the plaintiffs for cancellation of
the sale deeds dated 16.01.2009, 08.5.2013 & 01.5.2014
as well as the injunction against the last purchaser
Shri Prashant Arora to maintain the status quo on the spot
in question.
The plaintiffs are coming on the basis of entries
in the Khasra and Khatoni of the village Ganeshpur Khet
no. 389/1/2 on the land admeasuring 2886.50 square feet.
It is evidently clear from the record that this property is no
more agriculture one and for almost last 65 years, it has
been in the municipal limits and attained the municipal
numbers. It was previously occupied by the predecessors of
Shri Ayodhya Prasad (may be a licencee) but, with the
passage of time, it appears that in more than 50-60 years
their predecessors acquired adverse possession over the
same. Ultimately, they sold it on 16.01.2009 to Shri
Yogendra Singh-defendant no. 2, who in turn, executed a
sale deed of the same property on 08.5.2013 to defendant
nos. 3 & 4 (Anubhav Tyagi and Rahul) and such
defendants further sold it to Mr. Prashant Arora.

2
In some sale deeds, it has been mentioned as the
ancestral property in the form of the house. In yet another
sale deed, it mentioned as a vacant plot of land. The area of
389/1/2, as has been sorted out by the learned Trial Judge
in the impugned order dated 19.12.2016, is only 2150
square feet. So, it is clear that the identity/area of the
property in question is in uncertainty so, there may be
some prima facie case of the plaintiff, which may ultimately
be deduced at the end of the trial but, the fact remains that
Shri Prashant Arora purchased the plot of land for huge
consideration after verifying the previous two sale deeds
executed in favour of previous vendors.
Therefore, so far as irreparable loss is concerned,
the appeal tilts in favour of Mr. Arora. So, the order of
maintaining the status quo by this court dated 23.12.2016
is hereby vacated. However, the suit for cancellation of the
sale deeds will continue and if, ultimately the plaintiffs
succeed then, Mr. Arora will remove his all constructions
and at the same time, the court also restrains Mr. Arora to
execute the further sale deed on the plot of land in question
but, he will be at liberty to augment its construction and to
live in on such property till the rights of the parties are
decided finally.
The appeal, thus, stands disposed of in the
above terms.
The learned Trial Court is also directed to
adjudicate the matter at the earliest and without granting
any unnecessary adjournment.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
 25.4.2017
Pooja/A.Kaur
